correctness.rationale: Coordinatewise min/max of two increasing embeddings are embeddings; a hybrid argument forces exactly one differing coordinate. Necessity and sufficiency of all m+2 gap restrictions follow from greedy first and last subsequence embeddings and adjacency-distinct target letters. Each fork index is uniquely recoverable, so the geometric-series products are disjoint and exhaustive. Direct coefficient extraction gives B(m+2) and the class invariant, and evaluating the unique dominant double pole proves the sharp asymptotic. Independently implemented exact enumeration and backtracking checked 534 instances across 1,472,158 hosts, but finite checks are not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2026 Bruda source treats exact general-alphabet single occurrences and structural all-frequency questions but not the displayed exact two-occurrence target-sensitive q-ary formula. Menon--Singh covers binary k=2, in which palindromic-return variation is impossible, and an earlier q=3, p=012 case is explicitly recognized as subsumed. The new complete classification by interior ABA triples and exact m-1 class census does not follow from those narrower claims. value.rationale: Exactly-two subsequence languages are a natural sharp multiplicity layer of word embeddings. The result completely partitions all adjacency-distinct q-ary patterns of any fixed length into m-1 distinct enumerative equivalence classes by a local ABA statistic, counts all patterns in each class, and determines every host-length coefficient and asymptotic constant. The phenomenon distinguishes ternary patterns 012 and 010 (20 vs 21 hosts of length five), whereas existing binary and exactly-one results cannot see this local distinction. This classification and fork grammar are structural rather than an isolated finite table.
